atoms.text: The area now known as Scotland was called Caledonia by the Romans.
They described several main tribes that lived there: the Caledones lived in the north-west, the Venicones in the north-east, the Votadini in the south-east, and the Damnoni in the south-west.
atoms.sound: They described several main tribes that lived there: the Kal-le dohnez lived in the north-west, the Vehni cohnez in the north-east, the Votadini in the south-east, and the Damnoni in the south-west.

end.text: Later, the Romans began using one name for many of these northern tribes: the Picti. This was Latin for “the painted ones” because the Picts, as we call them in English, decorated their bodies with paint.
end.sound: Later, the Romans began using one name for many of these northern tribes: the Pictey. This was Latin for “the painted ones” because the Picts, as we call them in English, decorated their bodies with paint.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in this Roman historian’s description of the Picts.

atoms.b: Similarly to the Britons, the Picts spend most of their days ((++farming singing)) and fishing.
They live in villages made up of ((++roundhouses skyscrapers)) built from wood, clay and thatch.
Peace is rare! When they aren’t resisting Rome, the ((++tribes cities)) war among themselves over land and livestock.

feedback.finish: Most of what we know about the Picts comes from Roman historians such as Tacitus, who described Rome’s expansion into northern Britain.

text: The Romans also brought new foods to Caledonia, such as cabbage, onion and cucumber.

instruction.text: Fill in the gaps in this Roman historian’s description of the Picts.

atoms.b: The Picts also kept livestock and ((++hunted haunted)) wild animals in the forests and highlands.
They made clothing from wool, ((++leather plastic)) and various animal skins and furs.
The climate in the north was often ((++cold hot)) and harsh, so they wore long cloaks to keep warm.

text: Stone carvings left by the Picts suggest that they may have also used falcons to help them hunt.
